newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Volvo June Japan car registrations fall.
newsitem.headline: Volvo June Japan car registrations fall.

text.p: Swedish vehicle maker AB Volvo said on Thursday that its car registrations in Japan fell by 13.3 percent in June from the same month last year to 2,213 cars.
So far this year Volvo has registered 10,697 cars in Japan compared with 13,025 cars at the same time last year.
"The decline is a direct impact of the general increase in consumption tax in Japan in April," company spokesman Ulf Thorne told Reuters.
Japan's consumption tax was raised to five percent from three percent on April 1.
"We think that this increase has hit the big car sector, which includes us, particularly hard. We have still done better in June than our rivals and have increased market share."
"Many people who wanted to buy a car did so before this happened. I think in fact that the month before the consumption tax was raised was our best month ever in Japan," Thorne said.
Volvo said it expected the large car market in Japan to become brighter in coming months. "We expect to see a recovery in coming months," Thorne said.
"We put in the S40/V40 in the autumn and will also present the S40 Turbo. We will launch a campaign with the V70 RAWD together with a jubilee version of the 940.
"We are to also introduce the V70 XC. It will come to Japan and the U.S. as its first markets in the autumn. This is a model that we really believe in," he said.
